first_summary: README.md still carries the old landscape throughout. It says the Agent tool has no effort parameter, treats Haiku as an effort-less 4.5 tier shipped without an `effort:` line, and bases the whole 1x/2x/4-5x/10x output-cost ladder on a Haiku 4.5 baseline with an Opus 4x/5x "range" that the opus alias no longer spans. The rot sits in five places: the lever table, the tier table's effort and cost columns, footnote 1, the multiplier paragraph under the tiers, and the layout comment for the effort-grid file. What survives is the frontmatter-effort mechanism, the model/effort of each pinned tier, inherit-means-session-model, and the advisor attaching to every tier. The savings-only framing is milder and mostly low-confidence.
critic_summary: The first pass was thorough on the stale numeric and haiku claims in README.md and I found nothing to dispute. It missed the "effort choice actually reachable" framing at L12, the section heading at L15, the "rather than a saving" objective framing at L131, and several still-true-keep rows (worker, inspector, reviewer, judge, advisor attachment).
